## The bug

`entire doctor` printed this for a repo whose checkpoint sync election had **failed closed** — `strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote` naming a remote that does not exist, so no push carries checkpoint data at all:

```
Checkpoint destination: REVIEW
  This repo has 2 remotes (origin, publish).
    Checkpoints sync to a single elected remote — not to whichever one you
    push to. A push to any other remote carries your code but no session
    history. Run `entire status` to see the elected destination and how many
    checkpoints are waiting for it.
```

There is no elected destination, and `entire status` says `! Checkpoints NOT syncing`.

**A second half, which is worse:** the note fires only on *ambiguity* (>1 unpinned remote, or a fan-out remote). In the ordinary one-remote repo with the same typo, `entire doctor` said **nothing at all** about sync being off.

The cause is that `remote_topology.go` inspects remotes and settings but never calls `strategy.ResolveCheckpointSyncRemote` — it states the election's rules rather than its verdict. That is the same defect the note was already fixed for once: `TestMultiPushURL_DestinationNoteSurfaces` pins that it no longer claims checkpoints "follow whichever remote you push to".

## The fix

`remoteTopology` now consults the resolver, for the same reason `pinned` already asks it rather than reading settings. When the election has failed closed it reports that instead of the destination narration, and it reports regardless of ambiguity, which closes the silent one-remote case. The two conditions are exclusive: while sync is off there is no destination to describe, and the ambiguity paragraphs all narrate where checkpoints land.

```
Checkpoint sync: DISABLED
  checkpoint_push_remote names "gone", which is not one of this repo's remotes,
  so nothing is elected to carry checkpoints.
  Affected remotes: origin, publish
  Pushes to them carry your code but no session history, which stays in
  this clone.
  Fix: remove strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote to let Entire elect one,
  or point it at a remote this repo actually has.
  A remote name is a per-clone fact: prefer .entire/settings.local.json, since a
  committed one disables checkpoint sync in every clone that lacks that name.
```

The `settings.local.json` line is deliberate. A committed `checkpoint_push_remote` fail-closing for a teammate whose clone lacks that remote name is the most likely way this reaches a user, and `hintGatedCheckpointSync` already makes the same argument for the same reason.

The fail-closed return becomes `CheckpointPushRemoteNotConfiguredError` (typed, matched with `errors.As`; message byte-identical, so `entire status` output is unchanged). It exists so a caller can tell the misconfigured setting from the *other* fail-closed outcome — an unreadable settings file — and attach the remedy that fits. An unmatched cause gets no remedy, per the rule the `.entire` directory errors follow.

A remote pinned to a dedicated `checkpoint_remote` URL is exempt from the whole report, because the pre-push gate exempts it from the election (`ps.hasCheckpointURL()`) before consulting it, so its checkpoints really do still ship.

## Two calls a reviewer should make rather than inherit

**`entire enable` gained this report, not just the correction.** Fixing the false paragraph in the shared note was unavoidable for both callers; printing the *disabled* block on enable is an addition beyond the reported defect. It seemed right — a committed setting naming a remote this clone lacks is specifically a clone-time condition, which is exactly when `enable` runs — but it is one paragraph of new output on another command, and easy to scope back to doctor-only.

**`status` and `doctor` now disagree in dedicated-`checkpoint_remote` mode.** `status` warns there anyway, under a documented "Accepted divergence" whose stated premise is that "there is no elected remote left to probe `PushURL` against". This change shows that premise is false: probing per-remote needs no election. I left `status` alone because changing it is a product call, but the divergence looks retirable rather than inherent, and two commands disagreeing about "is my session history syncing" is not a great place to leave it.

## Tests

Six unit tests in a new `remote_topology_test.go` (the file had none), each asserting the **false** phrasings are absent rather than only that the new text is present, plus a coverage case for the remoteless branch. Mutation-checked: forcing `syncDisabled()` true fails three of them, so they are not vacuous. `TestCheckpointSyncRemote_MisconfiguredSettingFailsClosed` — which already builds exactly this repo on both backends — gains the wiring assertion that only a real repo can make.

`mise run check` passes (fmt, lint 0 issues, unit + integration + Vogon canary), plus `GOOS=windows go vet ./...`.

## Follow-ups, deliberately not in scope

- **The success arm still restates precedence rules** instead of printing the elected remote the topology now has in hand. `git log` shows this paragraph rewritten three times in five weeks, each time because a hand-maintained restatement went stale — and the previous rewrite's message explicitly considered using the resolver's answer and chose to point at `entire status` instead, which is what produced this bug. Naming the remote inline would end the cycle, but it changes output outside this defect and an existing integration assertion.
- **`hintGatedCheckpointSync` still says nothing on stderr at push time**, which is the moment the data is actually dropped; both commands fixed here require the user to think to run them. Unlike the ordinary gated-sync hint, the advice is unconditionally correct in this case, since a missing remote is wrong for every push target.
